To show another application, during the "day of the spirits" <note>the 14th or 15th of the lunar month</note>, on a cloth from a cemetery, using charcoal from a cemetery, one should draw the form of **Yamāntaka** inside a union-box <note>two bowls joined together</note> while reciting a hundred and eight times. Having interspersed the name in his heart, preceded by the recitation of the mantra, the practitioner—the yogi who recites the interspersed mantra "Idam dāpaya hrīḥ svāhā" <note>give this [to me], Hrīḥ Svāhā</note> for a specific person a hundred and eight times—will bestow the desired results upon others. Through the phrase "this very mantra" and so forth, one draws the image of the enemy with charcoal on a cemetery cloth. At midday or midnight on the day of the spirits, with the form and mind of a wrathful deity and the thought of sharp weapons, one begins from the head and touches the center down to the circle of the feet. The text shows "the enemy will be stopped" <note>killed</note>. Through the phrase "the hammer" and so forth, one makes an image of the object to be accomplished using the dust from the enemy's feet and earth from both banks of a river. At the previously explained time, the practitioner of **Yamāntaka**, having become angry and reciting the syllable **Phaṭ**, brings the hammer down on its head. At that time, it is shown that "by the hammer falling on the head in actuality, they will be deprived of life." Alternatively, "all these should also be done through meditative absorption," meaning they are performed by meditative concentration alone, so that one does not depend on external substances. Through "Hūṃ" and so forth, one imagines oneself as the King **Vajra-Subjugator** <term>Nīlāmbaradhara-Vajrapāṇi</term> from the transformation of the **Vajra Mind**. In one's own hand, from the transformation of the syllable **Hūṃ**, one imagines a fierce vajra with a garland of flaming **Hūṃ** syllables. As before, one should bring it down on the head of the image of the object to be accomplished. This shows the lack of dependence on external substances. At that time, it is shown that the performance of those activities of theirs is "meaningless." Regarding the phrase "to show other applications," and so forth: on a <term>bhuta</term> <gloss>spirit</gloss> day, on a cloth from a cemetery, use charcoal from a cemetery to <insert>recite one hundred and eight times inside a joined vessel</insert>. Draw the form of <term>Yamāntaka</term> <gloss>the Destroyer of Death</gloss> and place the name <note>of the target</note> within his heart. Preceded by the recitation of the mantra, for the person named "So-and-so," recite the mantra <term>IDAṂ DA PAYA HRI SVĀHĀ</term>. It is shown that for the practitioner who recites this one hundred and eight times, the desired results will be granted upon the others.

Regarding the phrase "this very mantra," and so forth: draw the likeness of an enemy with charcoal on a cloth from a cemetery. Place the name in its heart. At either midday or midnight, on a <term>bhuta</term> day, with the appearance of a wrathful deity and a wrathful intention, and with the thought of a sharp weapon, touch the center <note>of the drawing</note> starting from the head down to the <term>mandala</term> <gloss>circle</gloss> of the feet. It is shown that by doing so, "the enemy will be stopped."

Regarding the phrase "hammer," and so forth: use the dust from the enemy's feet and earth from both banks of a river to make a likeness of the target. At the previously mentioned time, while maintaining the <term>yoga</term> <gloss>spiritual discipline</gloss> of <term>Yamāntaka</term>, become enraged and recite the syllable <term>PHAT</term>. If one strikes the head of the image with a hammer, it is shown that "at that moment, in reality, the hammer falling on the head will cause the enemy to be parted from life."

Alternatively, the phrase "all of these should also be done through meditative concentration" means they can be performed through <term>samādhi</term> <gloss>meditative absorption</gloss> as well. By doing so, one "will not depend on external substances." Regarding the phrase <term>HUM</term>, and so forth: from the total transformation of the Mind Vajra, imagine oneself as the King <term>Guhyasamaja</term> <gloss>Secret Assembly</gloss>. As before, strike the head of the target's likeness; by this, it is shown that there is "no dependence on external substances."
